problems.memo_sentence: They also report that clustering 170 assets with k = 10 on current D-Wave hardware took over 10 minutes wall-clock time due to practical access overheads, and claim this is, to their knowledge, the first demonstration of a quantum advantage in solution quality for asset clustering on real quantum hardware.
problems.source_evidence: This work is the first, to our knowledge, to demonstrate a quantum advantage in solution quality using real hardware for the practical task of asset clustering, validated on both synthetic and real financial data.
problems.explanation: The source claims a quantum advantage 'using real hardware', without specifying 'real quantum hardware'; the memo adds 'real quantum hardware' and 'for asset clustering' in a way that is slightly more specific than the source text. This is a mild tightening of the claim beyond the exact wording given.

problems.memo_sentence: GCS-Q is robust to real-world scenarios with heterogeneous cluster sizes and avoids the idealized constraints (e.g., uniform clusters, ternary edge weights) assumed in prior work [4,6].
problems.source_evidence: GCS-Q is robust to real-world scenarios with heterogeneous cluster sizes and avoids the idealized constraints (e.g., uniform clusters, ternary edge weights) assumed in prior work [4,6].
problems.explanation: While this sentence in the paper is itself somewhat strong, the memo elsewhere treats robustness as clearly established. The experimental section only evaluates heterogeneous sizes in noise-free synthetic graphs and on one 50-asset real dataset, so treating robustness as a broad, fully demonstrated property is a bit stronger than what the limited experiments can justify.

problems.memo_sentence: In their synthetic experiments, no noise is added, so results reflect idealized structural conditions rather than realistic market noise.
problems.source_evidence: No noise is added, isolating algorithmic behavior under ideal structural conditions. We extrapolate the setup later in Sec. 3.2 to evaluate robustness under noise.
problems.explanation: The memo notes the lack of noise in synthetic experiments but omits the authors' statement that they 'extrapolate the setup later in Sec. 3.2 to evaluate robustness under noise,' i.e., they intend some assessment of robustness via the real-data experiment. Leaving this out slightly overemphasizes the synthetic-data idealization without acknowledging how the authors try to mitigate it.
